title: Brake, Steering and Suspension Service
author: Erudior
description: Compare disc and drum brakes, calipers, master cylinders, steering gears and assist systems. Inspect a physical wheel end and document its measured condition. Includes a parts atlas and an assessed modification workshop.
changelog: Added two in-depth cases, four assessed questions, two study cards and a practical evidence record. A repeatable hub/rotor runout trace and a separate thickness map.

lessons.title: Follow brake force and track a loose wheel
lessons.body:
Entry skills: complete Workshop Measurement and Vehicle Service, or demonstrate the equivalent workshop skills.

Pedal force acts on the master cylinder. Fluid pressure acts on caliper pistons, pads clamp the rotor and friction creates wheel torque. The tire-road contact limits how much force reaches the ground. Steering and suspension joints constrain wheel motion. Movement measured at the wheel can originate in several joints, so watch the joint as the trainer is moved.

## Worked shop case

Pressure of 2 N/mm² acting on one 300 mm² piston produces 600 N at that piston. This is piston force. Calculating road force would also require clamp geometry, friction, effective radius and tire radius.

## Guided practice

Pressure of 3 N/mm² acts on one 200 mm² piston. What piston force results in newtons?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

**What you will produce.** An inspected physical wheel end and its completed measurement and disposition sheet.

Identify individual components in the parts atlas and trace their interfaces on your exact donor drawing.

lessons.title: Disc and drum brakes, master cylinders and brake assist
topics: Disc and drum brakes, master cylinders and brake assist
lessons.body:
A master cylinder converts pushrod force to hydraulic pressure. At fixed input force a larger master piston lowers pressure but displaces more volume per unit travel. A booster adds force by vacuum, hydraulics or electric actuation. A split hydraulic system limits what a single circuit failure can affect. ABS valves and a pump intervene in pressure control. Electronic parking brakes and regenerative blending add controls and service modes that must be identified before work.

In a floating disc caliper, reaction moves the caliper on guides to apply the outer pad. In a fixed caliper opposed pistons apply pads on both sides. A drum uses shoes against its inner surface and can obtain self-energizing action from rotation depending on geometry. Compare heat dissipation, parking mechanism, inspection access and adjustment. Lateral rotor runout, rotor thickness variation and minimum thickness describe three different measurements. Select the correct test and component-specific discard limits.

## Worked shop case

Inner and outer pads on a floating caliper have very different wear. Guide movement, pad supports, piston release and hose condition merit investigation; contrasting wear alone cannot select one cause. On a fixed caliper inspect the opposed pistons and pad freedom. Do not invent a guide-slide test for a caliper bolted rigidly in place.

## Guided practice

```example fade=2
problem: At fixed pushrod force a training master doubles its piston area. What follows?
step: Divide the force by the new area.
step: Compare displaced volume at equal stroke.
answer: Pressure halves and volume per fixed stroke doubles. No installation recommendation follows from this calculation alone.
```

## Independent shop or design task

Identify the installed caliper or drum architecture, parking brake, assist type and hydraulic split from the donor drawings. Perform the course wheel-end inspection with the appropriate dust controls and measure the specified features.

Record the selected component, alternative, source and measured result in your component record. Identify open items for the design or practical reviewer.

lessons.title: Steering gears, column, linkage and assist
topics: Steering gears, column, linkage and assist
lessons.body:
A rack directly converts pinion rotation to lateral travel and moves tie rods. A recirculating-ball steering box commonly rotates a sector shaft and pitman arm to drive external linkage. Linkage slack, joints, mounts and column couplings can each contribute to steering free play. Mechanical steering ratio relates steering-wheel angle to road-wheel angle under defined conditions. Variable ratio, Ackermann geometry and compliance can change a measured result across the travel.

Hydraulic power steering uses a pump, lines, control valve and actuator; check fluid, leakage, belt or pump drive and pressure/flow under specified conditions. Electric power steering adds a torque sensor, controller and assist motor at the column or rack. A loss of electrical assist may involve supply, sensor plausibility or a controller fault. Rack mounting, inner-pivot location, collapsible column, shaft joints and alignment must agree with the chassis and suspension through their travel.

## Worked shop case

Two racks share mounting-hole spacing but have different inner tie-rod pivot widths. At ride height both can be adjusted to the same static toe. During bump their tie rods swing on different arcs, so measured toe curves can differ. Select using the loaded geometry and measured travel as well as the bolt pattern.

## Guided practice

```example fade=2
problem: A teaching steering wheel turns 240° for 15° at the stated road-wheel reference. Estimate the steering ratio.
step: Use angles measured over the same interval.
step: Divide wheel angle by road-wheel angle.
answer: The average is 16:1 over this interval. Verify the rest of the travel separately.
```

## Independent shop or design task

Map the complete donor path from steering wheel to knuckles. Record power or hydraulic interfaces, mount locations, joint angles, travel stops and the way that free play and toe change will be measured.

Record the selected component, alternative, source and measured result in your component record. Identify open items for the design or practical reviewer.

lessons.title: Design a rotor measurement map
lessons.body:
Rotor thickness variation and lateral runout describe different quantities. Measure thickness at equal radius around the disc with a suitable micrometer. For runout, secure the disc as specified and measure lateral indicator travel as it turns. Clean mounting faces and identify the exact model's limits before interpreting either test.

## Worked shop case

Four thicknesses at equal radius span 22.01–22.05 mm. Variation is 0.04 mm. Minimum thickness requires a separate comparison with the actual discard limit.

## Guided practice

Thickness varies from 24.12 to 24.18 mm. Enter variation in mm.

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## Your design

Use service data for a selected wheel end. Sketch four thickness points and the runout fixture. Give separate limits, units and dispositions for thickness, variation, play and runout.

```assignment
writing: design
```

## Component design review

Compare the candidates in the component register and bring your selected configuration into this design.

```assignment
writing: component-selection
```

Read a modification card, choose a baseline and identify the changed parts, including hardware and seals.

lessons.title: Separate hydraulic force from brake torque
topics: Separate hydraulic force from brake torque
lessons.body:
In a simplified hydraulic brake circuit, line pressure is force at the master piston divided by its area. The caliper converts pressure to piston force. Rotor effective radius and pad friction affect brake torque. A larger master piston moves more fluid per stroke but needs greater force for the same pressure. Pedal leverage, booster assistance, component stiffness, available travel and front-rear balance all enter an actual design.

**Worked comparison.** An idealized master is driven with 400 N and has 200 mm² of area. Pressure is 2 N/mm², or 2 MPa. Doubling the area at the same force halves pressure. At the same stroke the larger piston displaces twice as much fluid. A bigger caliper kit or different master can change pedal travel as well as force. Greater effective radius at the same tangential pad force increases torque, but tire grip, balance and ABS control still limit braking performance.

**Design review.** Trace the two circuits from the donor master to each wheel, including the ABS hydraulic unit. Label the piston and friction interfaces and the specified fluid. Compare stock and proposed components using manufacturer dimensions. Record bore, effective radius, wheel clearance, thermal capacity and evidence needed from a qualified reviewer. Use the calculation only to identify dependencies. A production brake change needs system-level validation.

lessons.title: Inspect a known-clean training corner
lessons.body:
Use a known-clean teaching assembly. Unknown brake and clutch dust needs appropriate controls. Identify tire condition, hose routing, pad wear, free movement and attachment points before disturbing the parts. Follow the service manual's limits, fastener rules, bleed procedure and functional checks if hydraulic service is undertaken by the shop.

## Worked shop case

A training rotor is stamped MIN 20.0 mm. The lowest repeatable measurement is 19.8 mm. Resurfacing would remove more material. Segregate this part from serviceable stock.

## Guided practice

A rotor's lowest reading is 21.30 mm against its 21.50 mm minimum. How far below minimum is it, in mm?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## US rules at the workbench

For covered employees performing brake or clutch work with potential asbestos exposure, use the controls and work practices in 29 CFR 1910.1001 and Appendix F for the operation. Use a known-clean training rig. Leave suspect dust undisturbed; dry sweeping or blowing it around the shop is inappropriate. Record the friction material's provenance and the controlled work method. Buy traceable hoses and brake fluid suitable for the intended vehicle.

[OSHA — brake/clutch asbestos controls, 29 CFR 1910.1001 Appendix F](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.1001AppF) · [NHTSA — equipment standards and a specific kit-manufacturer interpretation](https://www.nhtsa.gov/interpretations/19664ztv) · [HSE — working under supported vehicles, shop guidance](https://www.hse.gov.uk/mvr/mechanical-repair/under-vehicles.htm)

## Workshop preparation

Use a secured, unloaded training assembly. Leave unknown dust, loaded springs, airbag components and pressurized hydraulics to an appropriately equipped shop.

```assignment
lab: workshop
```

Bring the selected component record to the lab and enter what you personally inspected, made, measured or assembled, with the part identifier and actual conditions.

lessons.title: Measure repeatability before changing brake hardware
topics: Measure repeatability before changing brake hardware
lessons.body:
Open the parts atlas for this system. Trace a parent assembly into its named children and mounting hardware. Explain the function of each item, identify its controlling dimensions or interfaces, then decide which pieces you can machine or fabricate, which you can assemble and which to obtain as qualified assemblies. Put exact drawing or donor references beside your decision.

## Parts on the bench

Braking and steering, Friction, hydraulic and steering detail. The quick references linked below include the function, design, fabrication or installation route, and verification of every indexed item.

## Modifications to evaluate

- Pad compound and rotor package
- Brake cooling ducts
- Larger brake kit

## Worked example

At fixed vehicle mass, kinetic energy scales with speed squared. A stop from 80 km/h has four times the initial translational kinetic energy of a stop from 40 km/h. Temperature measurements taken after those two stops cannot isolate a duct's effect. Tire grip, brake balance and pedal condition also matter.

## Guided decision

```example fade=1
problem: A cooler rotor reading follows a run with half the vehicle speed. What must the next test hold constant?
step: Control mass, speed schedule, initial temperatures, airflow, braking conditions and measurement delay.
answer: Compare matched repeated-stop results at a controlled facility using the same method and instrument location.
```

## Independent workshop

Build an unpowered duct-to-wheel-end mock-up and safely sweep the rig. Record the tightest hose/steering clearance; a static exercise does not qualify brake performance.

Open a modification card for its design, build and test sequence. Record original and changed readings under comparable conditions. Separate physical evidence from predictions and document a safe rollback.

```assignment
writing: modification-record
```

lessons.title: Find the source of rotor runout on a bench hub
topics: Find the source of rotor runout on a bench hub
lessons.body:
Lateral runout is side-to-side movement at a chosen radius. Disc thickness variation is the change in thickness around the rotor, measured with a micrometer at the specified positions. One instrument trace cannot measure both. Rust or debris at the mounting face, hub movement or uneven mounting can distort a runout result. Inspect the mount and bearing condition before condemning the rotor.

**Worked trace.** An indicator on a properly mounted training rotor swings between −0.03 and +0.06 mm. Total indicated runout is 0.09 mm. Mark the high point on the rotor and the matching hub position. Re-index the rotor only if the trainer procedure permits, secure it using the same specified mounting method, and repeat. If the high point consistently follows the rotor, investigate the rotor. If it stays at the same hub position, examine the hub and mounting conditions. Combined sources can partly cancel, so measure the hub face when indicated.

**Independent work.** On a detached bench hub, record mounting conditions, gauge radius, high and low readings and index marks for two trials. Make a separate thickness map. Identify which observation would distinguish lateral wobble from thickness variation and decide against the exact service limit for that assembly. Do not infer roadworthiness from this bench measurement.

```assignment
lab: case-record
```

lessons.title: Verify a correction and record remaining limits
lessons.body:
A low or sinking pedal demands diagnosis. A rotor measurement alone cannot clear an entire braking system. For the teaching corner, reassemble to the manual and remeasure using the original setup. On a complete vehicle, professional checks also include leaks, firm pedal, reserve travel, fluid level, assist and a controlled functional brake test.

## Worked shop case

Disc runout drops after a mounting face is cleaned and the disc is secured correctly. The matched test supports a mounting influence. It does not explain an unrelated sinking pedal.

## Guided practice

An indicator ranges from −0.03 to +0.04 mm. Give total indicator travel in mm.

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## Practical sign-off

The sheet distinguishes thickness variation, lateral runout and joint play, each with its own evidence. Record actual measurements and the disposition of faults. Submit the physical evidence in the workshop record.

```assignment
lab: workshop
```

Close each build-relevant component row with its measured result, reviewer disposition or an identified open issue and retest. Transfer the accepted configuration to your capstone record.

Reconcile required, issued, installed and verified quantities against the physical assembly and mark unresolved items.

references.title: Component register and build evidence
references.body:
For this course examine Friction brake; Master cylinder and split circuits; Assist and parking brake; Rack, box and linkages; Steering assist and column. Document manufacturer, part revision, drawing, selection, applicable authority or service requirement, installer, measured result with units, and reviewer disposition. Begin in design and update after installation.

| Family | Candidate designs | What changes | What to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Friction brake | Disc / drum; fixed / floating caliper | Follow clamp or shoe force, guide movement, heat rejection and parking mechanism. | Measure applicable rotor thickness and runout or drum diameter against source limits. |
| Master cylinder and split circuits | Different bores and split layouts | Piston area trades pressure for displacement; the split defines the effect of circuit loss. | Draw both circuits and compare master travel and pressure using the approved design. |
| Assist and parking brake | Vacuum / hydraulic / electric assist; cable / electric parking brake | Assist energy, failure response and service mode differ. | Identify reserve and warning checks, required service mode and an independent holding check. |
| Rack, box and linkages | Rack-and-pinion / recirculating-ball steering gear | Gear output and linkage paths control toe changes, turning radius and available space. | Record free play, stops, static alignment and toe over travel. |
| Steering assist and column | Manual / hydraulic / column- or rack-electric assist | Supply, sensors, shaft joints and collapsible-column support must suit layout. | Diagram the steering path and document motion and clearance across the adjustment range. |

references.title: Braking and steering · Brake pedal and pivot to Caliper body and pistons
references.body:
For an actual vehicle, identify the exact model, part revision, operating conditions and source before using a specification. Course examples are teaching fixtures. Document the physical work you perform, your inspection measurements and any specialist operations. Preserve relevant emissions controls, required safety equipment and diagnostic functions. Determine requirements for the specific intended use and jurisdiction before committing to changes.

### Brake pedal and pivot

**Function.** Provide leverage and input travel.

**Design.** Choose ratio, sweep, pivot support and pedal spacing.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fixture a reviewed assembly and fit bushed pivot, return and stop.

**Verify.** Measure free play and travel and inspect adjacent control clearance.

### Brake booster

**Function.** Adds assist force.

**Design.** Match vacuum, hydraulic or electric source, pushrod and master interface.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit a matched approved booster and restore needed lines or calibration.

**Verify.** Check reserve, assist response and warning functions.

### Brake master cylinder

**Function.** Produces hydraulic pressure in multiple circuits.

**Design.** Match bore, stroke, volume, split and booster interface.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install matched unit and bleed in the prescribed sequence.

**Verify.** Verify no bypass, stable pressure/pedal and working reserve.

### Brake reservoir

**Function.** Holds fluid reserve and allows level monitoring.

**Design.** Match fluid, volume and vent sealing; provide service access.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit clean seals, level switch and approved cap.

**Verify.** Verify level change, cap fit and low-level indication.

### Hard brake pipe

**Function.** Transmits pressure along the chassis.

**Design.** Select approved material, diameter, flare type and fittings.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Practice flares on coupons then bend and support the specified tubing using proper tooling.

**Verify.** Inspect every flare seat and perform approved hydraulic leak/proof checks.

### Flexible brake hose

**Function.** Maintains pressure path to moving wheel.

**Design.** Match pressure approval, fittings, length, twist and full-travel clearance.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit approved assembly and orient locating tabs without twist.

**Verify.** Check at full steer, bump and droop and verify pressure integrity.

### Disc rotor

**Function.** Provides friction track and thermal mass.

**Design.** Match diameter, thickness, offset, ventilation and caliper clearance.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit compatible rotor on a clean flange without trapping debris.

**Verify.** Measure thickness, lateral runout and variation under the specified clamp.

### Caliper body and pistons

**Function.** Convert hydraulic pressure to pad clamping.

**Design.** Match swept area, piston area, pad shape and master displacement.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Use a qualified matched caliper and specified mounting hardware.

**Verify.** Check full pad contact, leak-free operation and release.

references.title: Braking and steering · Caliper slide pin to Parking brake actuator and cable
references.body:
For an actual vehicle, identify the exact model, part revision, operating conditions and source before using a specification. Course examples are teaching fixtures. Document the physical work you perform, your inspection measurements and any specialist operations. Preserve relevant emissions controls, required safety equipment and diagnostic functions. Determine requirements for the specific intended use and jurisdiction before committing to changes.

### Caliper slide pin

**Function.** Allows a floating caliper to center itself.

**Design.** Match clearance, boot material and approved lubricant.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Clean or replace parts as specified; seat boots and retainers.

**Verify.** Check free travel and pad wear symmetry.

### Caliper piston seal and boot

**Function.** Retain pressure and exclude debris.

**Design.** Match seal kit to piston bore, fluid and model.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Rebuild only approved calipers with clean correct seals and piston inspection.

**Verify.** Use prescribed pressure/leak and release checks.

### Brake pad and backing plate

**Function.** Transform vehicle motion into heat at the rotor.

**Design.** Select cold response, temperature range, friction compatibility and intended duty.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit approved matched axle set and hardware; follow specified bedding process.

**Verify.** Measure pad clearance/wear and evaluate repeated stops on controlled site.

### Bleed screw

**Function.** Provides high-point release for air and fluid.

**Design.** Match seat, thread and access in installed orientation.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit compatible screw and seal the seat per specified tightening value.

**Verify.** Check no leakage after bleeding and reinstall dust cap.

### Brake drum

**Function.** Provides internal friction surface for shoes.

**Design.** Specify diameter, maximum service limit, heat capacity and offset.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit rated drum after measuring actual diameter and shoe compatibility.

**Verify.** Check diameter, roundness and drag after adjustment.

### Wheel cylinder

**Function.** Pushes drum shoes apart hydraulically.

**Design.** Match bore, fitting, mounting and fluid.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit approved cylinder and secure correctly oriented shoes and hardware.

**Verify.** Inspect under boots as prescribed and perform leak check.

### Brake shoes, return springs and adjuster

**Function.** Apply, release and maintain working clearance in a drum.

**Design.** Match shoe orientation, spring set and left/right adjuster threads.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Reassemble with approved brake-dust controls and exact side-specific diagram.

**Verify.** Verify self-adjustment, release and parking operation.

### Parking brake actuator and cable

**Function.** Hold a parked vehicle independently of normal pedal command.

**Design.** Match lever or electric actuator, return and adjustment range.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Route cable away from heat and movement or initialize matched motor service mode.

**Verify.** Verify independent hold and complete release by approved procedure.

### ABS modulator

**Function.** Adjusts wheel-circuit pressure under controller command.

**Design.** Match hydraulic split, sensor format, coding and bleed routine.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Use a compatible complete unit and prescribed scan-tool bleed.

**Verify.** Check codes, base brake function and approved ABS verification.

### Steering wheel and hub

**Function.** Transfer driver torque to column.

**Design.** Match spline, clocking, airbag and electrical interfaces and occupant geometry.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install the matched approved assembly under the donor restraint procedure.

**Verify.** Verify centered position, lock movement and retained functions.

### Steering column and intermediate shaft

**Function.** Transmit input while accommodating collapse and packaging.

**Design.** Preserve designed collapse path, splines, joints and support spacing.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Use compatible column and qualified joints, keeping clamp bolts in their designed grooves.

**Verify.** Check binding, engagement and clearances across travel.

### Steering rack

**Function.** Converts rotation into tie-rod motion.

**Design.** Match ratio, travel, pivot width, mounts and assist strategy.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install centered rack with correct mounting and load-rated fasteners.

**Verify.** Measure stop-to-stop freedom, toe curve and steering center.

### Steering box and pitman arm

**Function.** Convert steering rotation into linkage movement on box layouts.

**Design.** Match sector spline, pitman indexing, linkage travel and mount stiffness.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit matched box and indexed arm to reviewed support.

**Verify.** Check free play, travel limits, interference and attachment.

### Tie rod and outer end

**Function.** Transfer rack or linkage travel to the steering arm.

**Design.** Choose thread engagement, taper, range and articulation.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit compatible joint and engage locking hardware; set toe using proper equipment.

**Verify.** Check taper seating, measured toe and articulation through travel.

### Hydraulic assist pump and hoses

**Function.** Supply fluid flow and pressure for steering assist.

**Design.** Match pump capacity, reservoir, relief, pulley and rated hose ends.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install matched hoses, support return and bleed using donor data.

**Verify.** Check leakage, temperature and assist under specified conditions.

### Electric assist motor and torque sensor

**Function.** Supply assist according to driver input and control logic.

**Design.** Match motor position, electrical demand and safety calibration.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install matched rack or column and perform approved initialization.

**Verify.** Verify plausible torque signal, center calibration and manual path.

### Brake shoe hold-down pin

**Design.** Match pin length, cup, spring and backing-plate configuration.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install matching hardware with correct brake tools and dust controls.

**Verify.** Verify cups locked and shoes move without fouling.

### Drum brake adjuster screw

**Function.** Maintains shoe-to-drum clearance.

**Design.** Match left/right handed thread and operating lever.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Clean or replace as specified and install correct side and orientation.

**Verify.** Check adjuster action and resulting shoe drag.

### Brake hose retaining clip

**Function.** Secures hose end in bracket without stressing rigid line.

**Design.** Match slot, hose groove and bracket thickness.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fully seat matched clip after locating the line fitting.

**Verify.** Check that fitting cannot rotate or move under suspension travel.

### Brake wear sensor

**Function.** Signals pad wear by the system's intended method.

**Design.** Match electronic loop or mechanical tab to pad position.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install matched sensor and protect harness from rotor, wheel and heat.

**Verify.** Check warning diagnostics and retained routing.

### Brake-light switch

**Function.** Signals pedal application to lamps and controllers.

**Design.** Match switch logic, location and pedal free-play relationship.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit and adjust to exact donor reference without preloading the pedal.

**Verify.** Check all stop lamps, release and relevant controller inputs.

### Brake vacuum check valve

**Function.** Maintains booster reserve against reverse flow.

**Design.** Match orientation, bore, vacuum source and hose rating.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit the specified valve into a sound grommet and reinforced vacuum line.

**Verify.** Check one-way and reserve function by approved procedure.

### Steering rack bellows

**Function.** Keep contaminants away from rack and inner joints.

**Design.** Match rack travel, length and vent or equalization path.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit appropriate clamps without twisting the boot on centered steering.

**Verify.** Inspect both ends through full steer for pull-off and folding.

**Function.** Allows the inner tie rod to articulate as the rack moves.

**Design.** Match thread, load class, locking and pivot-center geometry.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit matched joint with specified housing support and locking feature.

**Verify.** Check axial play, toe setting and full-travel movement.

**Purpose.** Manage fade, response or wear in a specified duty cycle.

**Design and baseline.** Start with tires, existing hydraulic condition and repeatable symptoms. Compare cold bite, useful temperature range, rotor capacity, compatibility, dust, noise and road-use status.

**Purpose.** Improve repeated-stop heat management when logged data identifies a thermal limitation.

**Design and baseline.** Plan inlet, flexible route, articulation, safe mounting and delivery toward a suitable vented rotor inlet for the designed rotor. Protect steering, tire, hose and ABS routing.

references.title: How to account for every installed part
references.body:
# Build-specific parts reconciliation

The teaching atlas lists common light-vehicle parts and service assemblies across multiple architectures. A gasoline manual, a diesel automatic and a battery-electric car have different inventories. The as-built bill of materials establishes what **your particular car** contains, down to separately installed hardware. Start with the actual model year, market, engine, transmission, option codes and donor/source identity. Mark privacy-sensitive paperwork for private instructor review.

1. Make a system tree for the exact vehicle. Give each parent assembly an ID. Identify the source of every child from a dated OEM parts catalog or exploded figure, engineering drawing, kit packing list, supplier specification, harness diagram or direct teardown. A commercial catalog is good for identity and fitment. Use separate authoritative service data for torque, installation and test limits. For original parts, assign drawing numbers and revisions yourself.
2. Start a line in As-Built-BOM.csv for each **part at each installation position**, including each clip, washer, spacer, seal, terminal, retainer, ground strap, hose end, fluid charge, service label and replacement-only fastener. Split left/right, front/rear, orientation and hardware stack order; link each to its parent. A separate serialized component gets its own instance. Account for consumables retained on the finished part, e.g. coating or sealant by product, batch and measured or specified amount where applicable. Mark discarded assembly aids separately.
3. Tie every row to an approved configuration. Record exact part/revision, the number or amount required, received or made, installed and independently verified, with units. Compare numbers at that installation position; purchased spare stock belongs to inventory, not installed quantity. Add any part missing from the teaching atlas. Mark a nonapplicable teaching family with the architecture-specific reason. A missing source entry is an open item.
4. Distinguish **make** (original or drawing-controlled part), **assemble** (purchased parts you personally integrated), **buy** (approved component) and **specialist** (named service or operation). Record material, tooling, process, measured features or supplier documents and who inspected it. Document critical work before it is hidden. Preserve service access and replace-only rules.
5. For a sealed bought assembly with no serviceable internal list, identify its make, model, revision or serial where available, supplier and functional boundary. List every separately fitted connector, seal, mount and fastener. If the manufacturer publishes a serviceable breakdown or you rebuild it, expand the children you actually service. Leave inaccessible internal details marked as supplier-controlled. Do not dismantle restraint inflators or sealed traction assemblies for an inventory exercise.
6. Reconcile from both directions. Walk each drawing callout into the build ledger, then walk each real installed item back to a drawing, receipt, material record or revision. Have a second person inspect quantities, location, retention and test evidence. Mark each row accepted, absent by design, awaiting evidence, rework or spare. Release a function only when all its relevant rows and measured acceptance tests have passed. Record who accepted the change. The complete car still requires the existing witnessed commissioning demonstration and its intended-use approvals.

## Worked example

The SP-01 removable-plate fixture drawing calls for one plate and one fastener/washer stack at each of two identified positions. Its practice board supplies tapped holes. The separate example CSV includes eight rows. They identify the board, the plate, two labeled mounting positions as parent groups, and the two screws and two washers distributed under those groups. Parent groups carry no physical quantities. A missing right washer is an intentional open finding. Correct the installed count only after fitting the washer; update verified count only after reinspection. Accepting the measured board and plate as individual parts leaves fixture release on hold until the corrected right stack is verified. An unused spare remains a stock item.

## Graduation review

Turn in the assembly tree, marked exploded views, drawing revisions, actual bill of materials, inspection evidence, change records and final service schedule. Account for every called-out or observed item and every receiving/installation discrepancy. An instructor must be able to pick an item on the physical car, identify who made or fitted it, locate its source or released drawing, and see how it passed the appropriate acceptance check. A passing written exam cannot certify workmanship, registration, emissions compliance or crashworthiness.

writing.title: Design a wheel-end inspection sheet
writing.prompt: Use service data for a selected wheel end. Sketch four thickness points and the runout fixture. Give separate limits, units and dispositions for thickness, variation, play and runout. Include a labeled drawing or table in the work record and identify the applicable shop or legal requirement.

writing.title: Component selection and evidence
writing.prompt: For this course examine Friction brake; Master cylinder and split circuits; Assist and parking brake; Rack, box and linkages; Steering assist and column. Identify each applicable family on your own vehicle or donor and explain absent families. Use two identified alternatives for at least one consequential choice. Show the job each design performs, how its operating principle differs, one failure mode and a test that separates the alternatives. Identify a real model or part number for each shortlisted candidate. Compare a sourced limit or performance figure under common conditions, interfaces, legal or shop implications and service access. Defend your choice and explain one change that would reverse it. Link your drawing and physical observation or measurement to the build record.

writing.title: Workshop record · Measure repeatability before changing brake hardware
writing.prompt: Build an unpowered duct-to-wheel-end mock-up and safely sweep the rig. Record the tightest hose/steering clearance; a static exercise does not qualify brake performance. List your donor or drawing revision, part identities, position, material or rating, method, who made or fitted each item, and the governing source. State the goal, the baseline test, a controlled change, a potential adverse effect, comparable measured results, acceptance threshold and rollback. Include an attributable photograph, recorded direct observation or measurement. An inert prototype or mock-up qualifies for this comparison exercise when the vehicle modification requires specialist or legal approval. Identify exactly which vehicle results are still unproven.

labs.title: Inspect and reassemble a wheel end
labs.intro: An inspected physical wheel end and its completed measurement and disposition sheet. Plan shop time with your supervisor over the sessions the work actually takes.
safety: Use a secured, unloaded training assembly. Leave unknown dust, loaded springs, airbag components and pressurized hydraulics to an appropriately equipped shop.
materials: Known-clean training hub, rotor and steering joint
Micrometer and dial indicator with rigid stand
steps: Mark four measurement stations at the specified radius. Record thickness at each.
Mount the indicator and record minimum and maximum over a revolution. Repeat the setup.
Observe one joint under the manual's prescribed inspection and document where motion occurs.
Complete assigned reassembly and recheck. Keep any rejected or uncertain part tagged and out of service.

questions.prompt: What did you personally make or service? Record actual conditions, measured values, instruments, and any specialist operations.

The sheet distinguishes thickness variation, lateral runout and joint play, each with its own evidence. Record your result, corrections, retest and sign-off status. Include the witness name and date where required.
Which rule, authority or shop control applied at this site? Identify the actor, triggering operation, source and the record kept.

Name the actual part or trainer component and the design alternative you considered. Record the observed or measured result, units and conditions where applicable, and its effect on the as-built decision.
Identify one fitted part and each fastener, seal, clip or connector that you personally handled. Record parent assembly, position, source, required and observed quantity, and evidence.

labs.photos: Attach dated photographs of your own work, with part or revision identification. An instructor may also document direct observation.

labs.title: Find the source of rotor runout on a bench hub — workshop record
labs.intro: A repeatable hub/rotor runout trace and a separate thickness map.
safety: Secure the detached hub with the correct mounting procedure. Control pinch points; use the approved method for brake dust. Keep this bench measurement separate from a vehicle return-to-service decision.
materials: Detached bench hub and rotor, specified mounting hardware, indicator and rigid base, suitable disc micrometer
steps: Read “Separate hydraulic force from brake torque”. Prepare the marked drawing or schematic, acceptance source and prediction for your own case.

On a detached bench hub, record mounting conditions, gauge radius, high and low readings and index marks for two trials. Make a separate thickness map. Identify which observation would distinguish lateral wobble from thickness variation and decide against the exact service limit for that assembly. Do not infer roadworthiness from this bench measurement.
File the following evidence with the course project. A repeatable hub/rotor runout trace and a separate thickness map.

questions.prompt: Which variable, datum or condition did you hold fixed? Record the actual case and the evidence you personally collected.
Which observation changed or confirmed your initial decision? Identify an alternate explanation, the applicable acceptance authority, any unresolved limitation, and the reviewer/date.

labs.photos: Identify actual photos, annotated sketches, recorded trace IDs or a witnessed observation with the specimen, drawing revision and date.
